description: Focus the abelian-network bridge on the seed term r rather than on dynamics alone. Compute Smith-normal-form style invariants of the extracted relation lattice to remove seed generators that are redundant modulo the critical subspace, directly targeting the score numerator.
mathematical_formalization: Given a compiled candidate with relation lattice L_G \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^{2|V|}, solve \min |R_0| subject to \forall v\in V,\ (1,-1)e_v \in \operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{Z}}(L_G\cup R_0) and each generator in R_0 has singleton support drawn from X. Use Smith normal form of \mathbb{Z}^{2|V|}/L_G to expose residue classes that require explicit seeding.
analogical_connections: Critical-group residues act like stubborn defects that must be seeded away.
Seed compression resembles syndrome-basis minimization in coding theory.
The numerator m+r is treated as a budget, so algebraic redundancy is cashable immediately.
implementation_hypothesis: After any candidate motif is exactly extracted, compute a sparse integer basis for its relation lattice and run Smith-normal-form or modular reductions to identify indispensable singleton seeds. Then greedily or exactly minimize R while preserving full coverage of target singletons.
experiment_seed: Take the best 500 motifs from the odometer-guided ranking stage and measure how much r can be reduced without changing m, n, or t. Retain the idea only if the median reduction in r is material relative to total score.

closest_prior_art.title: Abelian networks III. The critical group

novelty_claim: The new element is an explicit algebraic compression objective for seed sets in arithmetic Kakeya certificates, driven by quotient-lattice structure rather than by ad hoc pruning.
differentiation: Critical groups are classical; what is not classical is optimizing the exact verifier score by using quotient-lattice information to compress singleton seeds under the user's legality rules.
